summary: Mark Siderits worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held emeritus professorships in philosophy at Illinois State University (~1979–2008) and Seoul National University (~2008–2013).

Mark Singleton specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Lakshmi Tatacharya, earned his PhD from the University of Cambridge (~2004–2008), and served as a Senior Research Fellow at SOAS University of London (~2015–2020).

Mark T. Unno works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Oberlin College (~1977–1981) and Stanford University (~1987–1994), later holding posts at Brown University (~1998–2000) and the University of Oregon (~2000).

Mark Tatz specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz (~1973–1978), also studying under several traditional teachers, and served as professor at the California Institute of Integral Studies (~1980–1992).
Mark Teeuwen specializes in Japanology and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. from Leiden University (~1990–1996) and became a professor at the University of Oslo around 1999.

Markus Viehbeck specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna (~2007–2012) under Helmut Tauscher and Franz-Karl Ehrhard, later working at Heidelberg University (~2012–2018) and the University of Vienna (~2018).

Marsha Weidner works in Sinology, art history, and Buddhist studies. After earning her Ph.D. from the University of California, Berkeley (~-1982), she held posts at the University of Virginia (~1984–1989) and the University of Kansas (~1989–2015).

Martha Nussbaum is a philosopher who studied at New York University (~1966–1969) and Harvard University (~1969–1975). She held academic posts at Harvard (~1975–1983), Brown University (~1984–1995), and the University of Chicago (~1995).

Martin Brauen specialized in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Zurich (~1968–1976), the University of Delhi (~1971–1972), and with several traditional teachers, serving as Konservator at the University of Zurich (~1975–2007).

Martin Collcutt specializes in Japanology and history. Educated at Fitzwilliam College, Cambridge (~1959–1962), and Harvard (PhD 1969), he taught at Yokohama National University and the University of Tokyo (1963–1969), before directing East Asian Studies at Princeton (1975–2015).

Martin Delhey specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Hamburg (~1993–2002, PhD under Lambert Schmithausen) and Kyoto, holding posts at Göttingen (2002), IIBS (~2003–2004), Ryukoku (~2004–2005), Hamburg (2002–2019), and Shandong (2019).

Martin Haug was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Rudolf von Roth and Theodor Benfey at Tübingen and Bonn. He held academic posts at Heidelberg, Bonn, Deccan College (~1859–1866), and the University of Munich (~1868–1876).

Martin Joachim Kümmel is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Eva Tichy and others at the University of Freiburg (~1991–1998) and took up a post at the University of Jena (~2011).

Martin King Whyte is a scholar of Sinology who studied at Cornell University (~1960–1964) and Harvard University (~1964–1971). He held academic posts at the University of Michigan (~1970–1994) and Harvard University (~2000–2014).

Martin Lehnert specializes in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Freiburg (~-2002) and became Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~2011).

Martin Lowenthal works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu, and he held academic posts at Boston College and Harvard University.

Martin Riesebrodt specialized in religious studies. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich and Heidelberg University (~1974–1980), later holding a post at the University of Chicago (~1990–2011).

Martin Seeger is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg (~1998–2004) under Barend Jan Terwiel and Lambert Schmithausen, and held a post at Hamburg from ~2002 to 2006.

Martin T. Adam specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and McGill University (~1996–2002, PhD under Richard P. Hayes), where he also served as an instructor.

Martin Willson was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. His training included studying under traditional teachers such as Thubten Yeshe (~1974–1984), Thubten Zopa Rinpoche (~1974), Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundub Sopa.
